text.p: These are the leading stories in the Botswanan press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Ministry of Mineral Resources and Water Affairs has distanced itself from a reported $7 billion project to set up an oil-from-coal project in Botswana.
Universal Investments has been granted a prospecting licence over the Mmambula coalfield, but not permission to mine.

- A former Nigerian diplomat, Daobu Nelson Gabriel Yellowe, has been found to have no valid residence permit and told to leave Botswana by December 10. He has reportedly lived in Botswana for 10 months after he left the diplomatic service.

- Marcus Thipe, a director of companies involved in a proposed $7 billion oil-from-coal project and an investment bank, says that despite being denied a banking licence for its Global Mining and Investment Bank, the group will go ahead with the project and will establish a bank.
